arxiv-2207-13985.title: An in silico -based review on anisotropic hyperelastic constitutive models for soft biological tissues
arxiv-2207-13985.creator: Hüsnü Dal, Alp Kağan Açan, Ciara Durcan, Mokarram Hossain
arxiv-2207-13985.description: Abstract We review nine invariant and dispersion-type anisotropic hyperelastic constitutive models for soft biological tissues based on their fitting performance to experimental data from three different human tissues. For this, we used a hybrid multi-objective optimization procedure. A genetic algorithm is devised to generate the initial guesses followed by a gradient-based search algorithm.

arxiv-2303-06506.title: Information propagation in long-range quantum many-body systems
arxiv-2303-06506.creator: Marius Lemm, Carla Rubiliani, Israel Michael Sigal, Jingxuan Zhang
arxiv-2303-06506.description: Abstract We study general lattice bosons with long-range hopping and long-range interactions decaying as | x − y | − α |x-y|^{-\alpha} with α ∈ ( d + 2 , 2 ​ d + 1 ) \alpha\in(d+2,2d+1) . We find a linear light cone for the information propagation starting from suitable initial states.

arxiv-2311-04541.title: Second-order Perturbative OTOC of Anharmonic Oscillators
arxiv-2311-04541.creator: Wung-Hong Huang*
arxiv-2311-04541.description: Abstract Abstract The out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC) of simple harmonic oscillator with extra anharmonic (quartic) interaction are calculated by the second quantization method. We obtain the analytic formulas of spectrum, Fock space states and matrix elements of coordinate to the second order of anharmonic interaction.

arxiv-2311-12780.title: Exact cube-root fluctuations in an area-constrained random walk model
arxiv-2311-12780.creator: Lucas D’Alimonte, Romain Panis
arxiv-2311-12780.description: Abstract This article is devoted to the study of the behaviour of a (1+1)-dimensional model of random walk conditioned to enclose an area of order N 2 N^{2} . Such a conditioning enforces a globally concave trajectory. We study the local deviations of the walk from its convex hull.

arxiv-2503-05260.title: Fair Center Clustering in Sliding Windows
arxiv-2503-05260.creator: Matteo Ceccarello, Andrea Pietracaprina, Geppino Pucci, Francesco Visonà
arxiv-2503-05260.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Matteo Ceccarello, Andrea Pietracaprina, Geppino Pucci, Francesco Visonà. The k k -center problem requires the selection of k k points (centers) from a given metric pointset W W so to minimize the maximum distance of any point of W W from the closest center. This paper focuses on a fair variant of the problem, known as fair center , where each input point belongs to some category and each category may contribute a limited number of points to the center set.

arxiv-2508-10849.title: Integrating Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial Networks for Sustainable 6G Operations: A Latency-Aware Multi-Tier Cell-Switching Approach
arxiv-2508-10849.creator: Metin Ozturk 1 , Maryam Salamatmoghadasi 2 , Halim Yanikomeroglu 2
arxiv-2508-10849.description: Abstract Sustainability is paramount in modern cellular networks, which face significant energy consumption challenges from rising mobile traffic and advancements in wireless technology. Cell-switching, well-established in literature as an effective solution, encounters limitations such as inadequate capacity and limited coverage when implemented through terrestrial networks (TN).

pmc-10606931.title: Sequence Analysis of the Malaysian Low Pathogenic Avian Influenza Virus Strain H5N2 from Duck
pmc-10606931.creator: Fatin Ahmad Rizal, Kok Lian Ho, Abdul Rahman Omar, Wen Siang Tan, Abdul Razak Mariatulqabtiah, Munir Iqbal
pmc-10606931.description: The avian influenza viruses (AIV) of the H5 subtype have the ability to mutate from low pathogenic (LPAI) to highly pathogenic (HPAI), which can cause high mortality in poultry. Little is known about the pathogenic switching apart from the mutations at the haemagglutinin cleavage site, which significantly contributes to the virus virulence switching phenomenon.

pmc-11286754.title: Biocatalysis enables the scalable conversion of biobased furans into various furfurylamines
pmc-11286754.creator: Pritam Giri, Seonga Lim, Taresh P Khobragade, Amol D Pagar, Mahesh D Patil, Sharad Sarak, Hyunwoo Jeon, Sangwoo Joo, Younghwan Goh, Seohee Jung, Yu-Jeong Jang, Seung Beom Choi, Ye Chan Kim, Taek Jin Kang, Yong-Seok Heo, Hyungdon Yun
pmc-11286754.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Biobased furans have emerged as chemical building blocks for the development of materials because of their diverse scaffolds and as they can be directly prepared from sugars. However, selective, efficient, and cost-effective scalable conversion of biobased furans remains elusive. Here, we report a robust transaminase (TA) from Shimia marina (SMTA) that enables the scalable amination of biobased furanaldehydes with high activity and broad substrate specificity.

pmc-12563986.title: Reducing Bias in the Evaluation of Robotic Surgery for Lung Cancer Through Machine Learning
pmc-12563986.creator: Alain Bernard, Jonathan Cottenet, Pascale Tubert-Bitter, Catherine Quantin, Nagio Takigawa
pmc-12563986.description: Simple SummaryConventional methods such as logistic regression for propensity score estimation often failed to adequately balance covariates, reducing the reliability of comparisons between robot-assisted surgery (RAS) and thoracotomy. Machine learning had been proposed as a potential solution, but its application in this context remained underexplored.

pmc-12749658.title: Synergistic effects of magnesium nano-oxide and mycorrhizal fungi on metabolite profiles in sesame (Sesamum indicum) under varying water regimes
pmc-12749658.creator: Marziyeh Rashidpour, Mostafa Heidari, Ali Rahmi Karizeki, Mehdi Baradaran Firouzabadi
pmc-12749658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study aimed to evaluate the effects of nano magnesium oxide (MgO NPs, OM2) and mycorrhizal fungi species, Funneliformis mosseae (MI2) and Rhizophagus irregularis (MI3), on sesame plants under different environmental conditions.

pmc-12904149.title: How to achieve low-carbon development in China: spatial spillover of education on carbon intensity
pmc-12904149.creator: Congying Ma, Hongchao Wu
pmc-12904149.description: IntroductionWith the looming global warming crisis, the question of how to achieve carbon neutrality is becoming an important issue confronting many countries. Although the spatial studies have indicated that education can spatially reduce the carbon intensity, they have ignored the transmission mechanism and dynamic interrelationship between education and carbon intensity.

pmc-13158295.title: Doxorubicin promotes the production of inflammatory cytokines in tumor-associated macrophages through activating lactate dehydrogenase A
pmc-13158295.creator: Bin Liu, Wei Yang, Shuo Feng, Xingning Jiang, Jingfan Lu, Fei Wang, Yaowen Hu, Yanhao Liu, Haifeng Ma, Ting Sun
pmc-13158295.description: Glioblastoma (GBM) presents a significant challenge because of its immunosuppressive microenvironment. The standard treatment protocol, including surgery, radiotherapy, and temozolomide, has been unable to alleviate immunosuppression. Doxorubicin chemotherapy induces immunogenic cell death in cancer cells, reshaping an immune-activated microenvironment. Here, we investigated the mechanism of immune activation induced by doxorubicin in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs).

pmc-13174969.title: Updated Genomic Epidemiologic Description of Candida (Candidozyma) auris, United States
pmc-13174969.creator: Lindsay A. Parnell, Amanda Ribeiro Dos Santos, Kaitlin Forsberg, Meghan Lyman, Elizabeth Misas, Lalitha Gade, D. Joseph Sexton, Anastasia P. Litvintseva, Nancy A. Chow
pmc-13174969.description: The multidrug-resistant yeast Candida (Candidozyma) auris has caused several healthcare-associated outbreaks in the United States. We provide a genomic epidemiologic description of 1,535 C. auris isolates collected in the United States during 2013–2022. We identified clades I, II, III, and IV but not clades V or VI.

pmc-13198291.title: Dual-targeted microspheres reshape the metabolic-immune microenvironment to reverse post-embolization dilemmas in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-13198291.creator: Nan Jiang, Zifan Pei, Fei Gong, Weihao Yang, Jiachen Xu, Jie Cao, Xiaoxiao Pan, Bin Yu, Jian Shen, Zhi Li, Binyan Zhong, Caifang Ni, Liang Cheng
pmc-13198291.description: SummaryTransarterial embolization (TAE) efficacy in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by post-embolization hypoxia-driven angiogenesis and metabolic reprogramming. To address this, we develop pH-responsive gelatin microspheres (GMs) encapsulating zinc sulfide (ZnS) nanoparticles (ZnS-encapsulated gelatin microspheres [ZnS@GMs]) for the dual delivery of hydrogen sulfide (H2S) gas and Zn2+ ions.

pmc-13521273.title: Structural adaptation associated with signaling preference at the human Growth Hormone–Releasing Hormone Receptor
pmc-13521273.creator: Ming-Wei Wang, Kaini Hang, Yue Qiu, Xianyue Chen, Yanyan Chen, Shengtian Huang, Zhaotong Cong, Qingtong Zhou
pmc-13521273.description: lemin et al., 1982; Mayo et al., 2003). GHRH secreted from the hypothalamus binds and activates GHRHR, evoking Gs-coupled cAMP signaling and stimulating growth hormone (GH) secretion, which governs systemic growth and lipid and protein metabolism (Granata et al., 2025).

pmc-13535889.title: Characteristics of the Health‐Associated Oral Microbiome in Young Nonhuman Primates
pmc-13535889.creator: J. L. Ebersole, O. A. Gonzalez
pmc-13535889.description: Nonhuman primates have been shown to develop periodontitis with clinical and demographic features similar to humans. This preclinical disease model is well‐positioned to advance the elucidation of novel biologic‐based preventive and therapeutic approaches to controlling periodontitis, a chronic infection and immunoinflammatory disease.

pmc-13588373.title: Twelve quick tips for designing AI-driven HPC workflows
pmc-13588373.creator: Jamie J. Alnasir
pmc-13588373.description: rtificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models across the life sciences has disrupted this traditional model. Unlike static pipelines, modern AI-driven configurations are inherently iterative, data-dependent, and probabilistic. They introduce structural cycles of model training, batch inference, validation, and automated refinement [1]. This operational shift changes the way AI-enabled workloads use cluster resources.
